invariants.rationale: The return value of the method directly reflects the boolean expression evaluated in the code.
If result is false, then scrollY must be true, based on De Morgan's law applied to the method's logic.
If result is false, then amountY < maxY must hold, since the only way for result to be false is for both scrollY to be true and amountY < maxY.
If result is false, then it must be because scrollY is true and amountY < maxY, but the only way for result to be true when scrollY is false is if !scrollY, hence this relationship.
Negating the method's logic gives an equivalent relationship for the result being false.
